conventions.convention: C[-1,1] consists of real continuous functions; P_n includes the zero polynomial; E_n is the infimum of uniform errors and Λ_n is the interpolation operator norm on the closed unit ball.
Degree n uses n+1 nodes: root angles (2j+1)π/(2n+2), and Lobatto angles jπ/n for n≥1. Both degree-zero families have the single node 0 and empty cardinal product 1.
Cosine arrays are decreasing; applying the increasing-node interpolation suppliers uses z_i=x_{n-i} with matching reversal of data and cardinal indices.
The cardinal quotient formulas exclude the matching node. Lobatto endpoint factors are c_0=c_n=1/2; interior factors are 1.
The logarithm is natural; the logarithmic estimate applies only for n≥1. Both degree-zero operator norms equal 1.

load_bearing.statement: Defines the two Chebyshev node families, cardinal interpolation operators I_n^σ, their operator norms Λ_n^σ, and E_n(f)=inf_{p∈P_n}‖f-p‖∞, including the degree-zero cases.

For either Chebyshev family and every n≥0, the cardinal polynomials have their prescribed Kronecker node values and are unique with degree at most n; I_n^σp=p for p∈P_n; Λ_n^σ=sup_{x∈[-1,1]}Σ_{j=0}^n|ℓ_{j,n}^σ(x)|.
For either Chebyshev node family, every n≥0, and every f∈C[-1,1], ‖f-I_n^σf‖∞≤(1+Λ_n^σ)E_n(f).

For n≥1 and θ∈[0,π] away from the matching node angle, |ℓ_{j,n}^R(cos θ)|=|cos((n+1)θ)|sin θ_j/((n+1)|cos θ-cos θ_j|); the Lobatto formula is c_j|sin θ sin(nθ)|/(n|cos θ-cos θ_j|), with half factors at endpoints.
For n≥1, Λ_n^R≤C log(n+1) and Λ_n^L≤C log(n+1), where C=4+(π+4)/log 2. For n=0, both one-node operators have norm 1.
For 0≤u≤π/2, sin u≥2u/π. For all real u,v, |sin u-sin v|≤|u-v|.
For every f∈C[-1,1], E_n(f)→0 as n→∞. This concerns best polynomial errors only and does not assert interpolation convergence at arbitrary node arrays.

seams_checked.note: Checked the cardinal definition, basis lemma, and interpolation uniqueness theorem against their uses. The decreasing Chebyshev arrays are explicitly reversed before applying the increasing-node suppliers; the one-node and zero-polynomial cases are preserved.

The coefficient theorem identifies the same Lobatto interpolant. Quadrature reproduction and near-best estimates use the stated all-degree interfaces, retain the midpoint degree-zero convention, and include the physical interval-length factor.

The collocation grid agrees with the descending Lobatto convention. The weighted near-best theorem faithfully cites the uniform bound for continuous real functions and N≥0, then applies the separate factor √π from the angular measure.
